svg.title: Small Enough to Understand
svg.desc: Sketch in perspective: a table with a shallow open tray on it, hatched, holding three small parts. In front of the table, one mannequin points into the tray; behind it, a second mannequin leans in and reaches for a part. Beside the tray, a dashed outline on the table top marks an empty space. The tray and its few parts are the system from the pattern's context: the hardware and software a group runs. Kept this small and open, it is the solution, the focus: a system small enough that everything can be seen at once. The pointing figure knows it; the reaching figure is a second member learning to run it, as the solution says, within a weekend. The dashed space is the solution's second half: room left for complexity, added only when a real need appears. The metaphor: a system as a tray of parts laid out on a table, not a sealed box only its builder can open.
